statement.p: Find the the general antiderivative F(x) of the function f(x) given below. Note that you can check your answer by differentiation.

static.solution: \int\,2 x^{5} \sin(x^{6})\,dx. We use substitution with w = x^{6} to find this. We have dw = 6\,x^{5}\,dx, so that \int\,2 x^{5} \sin(x^{6})\,dx = {1\over 3}\int\,\sin(w)\,dw = -{1\over 3}\,\cos(w) + C = -{1\over 3}\,\cos(x^{6}) + C.
